body:
## What to build

Preserve the row-shaped typed-missing prototype of a one-dimensional table column when it is omitted by a Grouping specification, so expansion can combine its original and omitted branches using the backend's ordinary type rules.

On main `28c449aa03fd5289916f0673e41c848cc126999e`, a local tibble holds the one-dimensional frequency table of observations a, b, b as one key column, with counts 1 and 2 and source-row identifiers 1 and 2. Included-only expansion and ordinary dplyr grouping both succeed. Expanding a rollup with a NULL Margin label and no Margin order instead raises vctrs_error_ptype2: “Can't combine `..1$key` <table[1d]> and `..2$key` <integer>.”

Ordinary mutation with a row-sized vec_init value followed by union_all succeeds: the key remains a one-dimensional table of four rows, with counts 1, 2, missing, missing, and each original payload row appears once in each Grouping-set occurrence. The package's scalar subsetting used for this prototype drops the table class and dimension before branch construction. A second independent fixture reproduced the successful control and failed expansion.

This is a prototype-construction defect, separate from the classed matrix/packed-dimension missingness-validation finding. A one-dimensional table is not covered by the matrix-only prototype branch, and its expansion still needs the correct prototype even if the validation finding is repaired. The NULL typed-missing label contract and ordinary dplyr/vctrs composition provide the expected behavior; no arbitrary attribute-restoration guarantee is requested under ADR 0016.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A rollup over the minimal one-dimensional table key with NULL or NA_character_ label and no Margin order returns the same key values, class, dimension, and payload multiplicity as the successful ordinary typed-missing mutation/union control.
- [ ] Cover empty and populated one-dimensional tables, omitted-first and included-first grouping-set order, retained duplicate occurrences, and optional public Grouping set identifiers.
- [ ] Included-only expansion continues to agree with the original input, and controls for ordinary atomic, matrix, packed, and factor keys keep their established behavior.
- [ ] Construct missing values through the backend's supported type rules without adding general attribute restoration or an unrequested read of a lazy input.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[The dated investigation](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/68f60d32a04e89a33151891698bd979dcda03508/investigation/expand-grouping-exhaustive-hunt-2026-10-30.md) records the pinned baseline, prototype inspection, independent witnesses, 216-case table/plain-array matrix, and limits. [The focused reproducer](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/68f60d32a04e89a33151891698bd979dcda03508/investigation/2026-10-30-expand-grouping-hunt/local/reproduce-table-prototype.R) has an intentionally failing assertion mode on the baseline; adjacent logs and classified CSVs are retained. The evidence is published in PR #1077; no implementation fix is included.

title: [P2] Preserve one-dimensional table prototypes during Margin expansion
